title: Shaboozey Rides ‘Western’ Concept Album Onto Multiple Billboard Charts
summary: The Outlaw Cherie Lee & Other Western Tales opens at No. 1 on Independent Albums, among other debuts.
body: Shaboozey ’s The Outlaw Cherie Lee & Other Western Tales debuts on multiple Billboard charts (dated Aug. 15), led by a No. 1 launch on Independent Albums. The set also starts at No. 3 on Americana/Folk Albums, No. 4 on Top Country Albums and No. 12 on the all-genre Billboard 200 with 31,000 equivalent album units earned in the United States from its release, on American Dogwood/EMPIRE, July 31 through Aug. 6, according to Luminate. The 20-track collection follows Shaboozey’s breakthrough Where I’ve Been, Isn’t Where I’m Going , which in June 2024 debuted at No. 1 on Independent Albums and Americana/Folk Albums and at its bests of No. 2 on Top Country Albums and No. 5 on the Billboard 200. It includes “A Bar Song (Tipsy),” which ruled Hot Country Songs for 45 weeks, the second-longest command in the chart’s history. A deluxe edition added the top 10s “Good News” and “Amen,” the latter with Jelly Roll. All hit No. 1 on Country Airplay. With Cherie Lee , Shaboozey goes all-in on the Western concept. The album tells the story of its fictional title character through songs and spoken-word vignettes, with Sam Elliott, Jamie Foxx and Teyana Taylor among those lending their voices. Le…

title: These 2 Demi Lovato Hot 100 Hits Have Just Gone 5x Platinum
summary: The singer received new RIAA milestones for two of her biggest hits as she returns to the Disney's Camp Rock 3.
body: “Cool for the Summer” just got a whole lot cooler. Demi Lovato has earned two new RIAA five-times Platinum certifications for the 2015 hit and fellow Confident track “Confident,” giving the singer another pair of milestones to celebrate as she returns to her Disney campgrounds in Camp Rock 3 . The tracks follow only “Sorry Not Sorry,” which was certified seven-times Platinum in December 2023, and “Heart Attack,” which was certified six-times Platinum in January 2026. title: The Biggest No. 2 Hot 100 Hits of All Time
summary: Though they fell short of the Hot 100's top spot, some No. 2 hits have generated cultural legacies that rival or even eclipse their chart-topping competition.
body: In his autobiography Q , Quincy Jones wrote, “Numbers 2, 6, and 11 are my least-favorite chart positions.” It doesn’t take a Jones-like genius to determine why. Despite a clear vote of public favor, each song that peaks at those ranks can come with a pang of disappointment as a song’s creators and performers just miss out on forever claiming a No. 1, top five or top 10 hit. Yet, particularly with No. 2-peaking hits, many of those narrow misses have evolved into iconic tracks with pop-culture legacies that rival or even eclipse their contemporary competition. Some – including a case a few years ago – sustain enough momentum to leapfrog No. 1 hits and become the year’s top Hot 100 single, others provide a springboard of momentum for artists to eventually capture that chart-topping hit on a subsequent try, and a select few dominate pop culture so strongly that you’d swear that they definitely, surely, undoubtedly topped the chart – before the facts reveal otherwise. While the No. 1s get plenty of shine, let’s celebrate another slate of hit singles that deserve a moment in the spotlight. title: Exceleration Music Signs Partnership With Christian Hip-Hop Label Reach Records
summary: The label, co-founded by Christian hip-hop artist Lecrae, will receive distribution from Exceleration Music's in-house distributor Redeye.
body: Exceleration Music has signed a strategic partnership with Christian hip-hop label Reach Records, home to artist and label co-founder Lecrae, Jackie Hill Perry and more. Through Exceleration’s in-house distributor Redeye Worldwide, the Atlanta-based Reach will receive global physical and digital distribution as well as marketing services to support its global expansion while retaining its “creative and operational independence,” according to a press release. The deal will extend Reach’s physical music business, expanding to retailers and direct-to-consumer channels globally. The agreement covers music released from 2026 onwards. title: Dwayne ‘The Rock’ Johnson Pivots to Music Career With Touching Girl Dad Ballad: ‘Your Dad’
summary: The burly wrestler-turned-movie-star, co-wrote the song from the Moana: Voices Across the Ocean album with 2023 American Idol winner Iam Tongi.
body: Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson is out to prove that he’s a very modern triple-threat kind of star. But in the former professional wrestler’s meaty hands, that trifecta includes body slams, acting and, based on his touching new pop ballad, singing. The burly movie star known for his bulging biceps and ping-ponging between intense action movies and family-friendly fare is firmly dipping his toe into the music world with the release of his sweet girl dad tune “Your Dad.” The song, co-written with 2023 American Idol winner Iam Tongi, appears on the brand new Moana: Voices Across the Ocean album, a companion to the recent big screen live-action Moana reboot. “My, my whole life changed/ From the moment I held you in my heart I knew/ That life would never be the same,” Johnson sings in a whispery voice over gently plucked acoustic guitar on the song whose video features home movies of Johnson loving on his three daughters. “Now you go move those mountains/ And sail across the oceans/ Go show the world and prove/ There’s nothing you can’t do,” he encourages them. title: Framework to Debut in Miami During Art Basel: ‘More Requests to Bring What We Do to Different Markets’
summary: Partnering with unKommon events, the show with ANOTR will mark the dance event producer's continued expansion out of SoCal.
body: Southern California-based independent dance event producer Framework is set to make its debut in Miami in December during Art Basel. Partnering with the Miami-based independent promoter unKommon events, Framework will host a Dec. 4 show with Dutch electronic duo ANOTR during the city’s week or art, music and parties. The Dec. 4 show will happen at a never-before-used venue at the city’s Watson Island Park, located on an island in Biscayne Bay between South Beach and downtown Miami. Tickets are available via Dice . Amsterdam-based duo ANOTR is on a continued hot streak, with its recent Ultra 54 collab “Talk to You” recently spending consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the WARM Global Dance Radio chart. Art Basel is a uniquely busy week for electronic music in Miami, with DJs and party brands touching down to be part of the action. Framework founder Kobi Danan tells Billboard that the company will set itself apart as “Just like anywhere we go, we’re going to do things our own way. title: The Longest-Leading Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s
summary: A select few hits have led the chart for at least 10 weeks.
body: Beginning with Debby Boone’s “You Light Up My Life” in 1977, a relatively select few smashes have led the Billboard Hot 100 for at least 10 weeks. How few? Just a mere 4% of all Hot 100 No. 1s dating to the chart’s launch on Aug. 4, 1958, have earned the achievement. Olivia Newton-John’s “Physical” flexed 10 weeks at No. 1 in 1981-82, and that smash and Boone’s shared the mark for the longest Hot 100 reign for more than a decade, until Boyz II Men’s “End of the Road” dominated for 13 weeks in 1992. That best lasted briefly, as Whitney Houston’s “I Will Always Love You” led for 14 weeks in late 1992/early 1993. In 1995-96, Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men’s “One Sweet Day” ran up 16 weeks at No. 1, a milestone that held for more than 23 years. (Songs began logging longer No. 1 stays after the Hot 100 adopted electronically tracked data, according to Luminate, in late 1991.) In 2017, Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee’s “Despacito,” featuring Justin Bieber, tied the No. 1 run of “One Sweet Day.” By 2019, Lil Nas X’s “Old Town Road,” featuring Billy Ray Cyrus, collected 19 weeks atop the Hot 100, a mark matched by Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” beginning in July 2024.
